headline: Sync holds: replays, retries, tombstones, edits, isolation and the Capture switch all behave, and nine of ten deliberate breaks went red. But the watchdog misses the case the brief tests it with (access revoked: no push for up to 48 h), and the suite’s own test of the 24-hour rule passes whichever rule fires.

suites.db: pgTAP 340 pass; API 168 pass, 10 skipped (GET routes in the write sweep)
suites.security: fail in the sweep (no gitleaks); pass with gitleaks 8.30.1 built from the Go proxy
suites.diff: 1 changed, 1 new, 0 check findings; 2 metrics flags (noise)

findings.title: Revoking notification access (or the listener being killed) brings no “Capture may be off” push for up to 48 hours after the last payment
findings.detail: The shell syncs a heartbeat every day whatever the listener’s state (`SyncWorker.scheduleDaily`, `SyncRun.buildBatch` puts `listenerConnected` and `access` in it). The server’s watchdog (`captureHealth`, apps/api/src/sync/health.ts) reads only the heartbeat’s *time* and the last event’s time: a fresh heartbeat that says `access: false, listenerConnected: false` counts as healthy. So the push waits for the 48-hour no-event limit, counted from the last payment. The brief’s done-when 5 says the watchdog fires “on the phone by revoking access for a day”, and `docs/local.md` B07 step 3 tells the owner to expect the push “by the next morning”: with a payment the evening before, it won’t come. In a browser, Home shows nothing either: `captureWarning` uses the phone’s own view only in the shell, and ignores the server’s `access`/`listenerConnected` (read in the code, not run). Home inside the shell does say *Capture is off*.
findings.repro: pnpm exec vitest run --config qa/B07/vitest.probe.config.ts -t "access revoked" (after pnpm test:db): a payment 20 h ago, then a heartbeat with access:false and listenerConnected:false, then the watchdog 10 h later.

access off, 30 h after the last payment: pushes 0; health {"on":true,"lastBeatAt":"2026-11-03T23:19:17.558Z","listenerConnected":false,"access":false,"lastEventAt":"2026-11-03T03:19:17.541Z","silent":null,"morningAt":null,"schedulerLate":false}
AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0

findings.title: The watchdog’s 24-hour heartbeat rule has no test with teeth: raising it to 72 hours leaves the suite green
findings.detail: sync.test.ts “pushes once a day when the listener has been quiet for a day” sets the heartbeat 25 h back, but the person’s events date from 1 Nov 2026, more than 48 h before the test runs, so the *no events* branch pushes the same title and the test passes whichever rule fires. It asserts only the title. Nothing else isolates the 24-hour rule, the one done-when 5 rests on.
findings.repro: In a worktree of HEAD: packages/core/src/sync.ts `HEARTBEAT_SILENT_MS = 24 * 3_600_000` → `72 * 3_600_000`; `pnpm test:db`.
findings.evidence:

Result: PASS
      Tests  168 passed | 10 skipped (178)
findings.spec: AC-20, §6.2 Health, B5; severity table: a test on a critical path that catches nothing

findings.title: *Captured on this phone* loses events that share a posted time at a page boundary
findings.detail: `GET /captured` pages by `posted_at < before`, and `next` is the last row’s `posted_at`. Rows with the same `posted_at` as the page’s last row are skipped on the next page. 51 events posted in the same millisecond: page 1 has 50, page 2 none. Ryt posts the same notification twice (the `duplicate` pair rule exists for it), so ties are plausible. Keyset on `(posted_at, id)` would hold them.
findings.repro: pnpm exec vitest run --config qa/B07/vitest.probe.config.ts -t "paging through 51"
findings.evidence:
ties: page 1 50, next 2026-10-10T02:00:00.000Z, page 2 0; distinct seen 50 of 51
AssertionError: expected 50 to be 51

findings.title: The no-events watchdog trusts the phone’s clock: an event stamped in the future silences it
findings.detail: `captureHealth` takes the newest `bank_events.posted_at` and the heartbeat’s `lastBankEventAt`, both from the phone. D143 (7) says the watchdog counts from the server’s clock. A phone whose clock ran a year ahead once keeps *no events* quiet for that year. Taking `created_at` (server time) for events would follow D143.
findings.repro: pnpm exec vitest run --config qa/B07/vitest.probe.config.ts -t "phone clock a year ahead"
findings.evidence:
future posted_at, 3 days without a real event: pushes 0
AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0

findings.title: The watchdog’s once-a-day guard isn’t held: keyed on the instant instead of the KL day, the suite stays green
findings.detail: The test ticks twice with the identical `now`, so an `alerts_sent` key per instant still dedupes there. Every real retry inside the morning window has a later `now`. The frame itself runs once a day (`tick-frame-reclaimed` is killed), so this is the second line of defence.

Result: PASS
      Tests  168 passed | 10 skipped (178)

findings.title: app_user can clear its own tombstone and back-date a heartbeat by direct SQL; only the API path guards them
findings.detail: `GRANT UPDATE (label, deleted_at) ON capture_apps` lets `UPDATE … SET deleted_at = NULL` revive a removed choice; the INSERT grant on `device_heartbeats` covers `created_at`. The API only writes through `sync_capture_app` and never passes `created_at`, so neither is reachable today. A later generic resource route over these tables would make them so.
findings.repro: psql sen_test, as app_user with app.user_id = B: UPDATE capture_apps SET deleted_at = NULL WHERE id = <B’s removed choice>
findings.evidence:
B revive own tombstone by UPDATE: ok, 1 rows
B heartbeat with own created_at: ok, 1 rows
findings.spec: §5 Sync can’t duplicate or undo; D143 (4), (7)

findings.title: The pull-down version is one counter for everyone
findings.detail: `sync_version` is a single sequence. A person who notes their version before and after their own change can count everyone else’s chosen-app changes in between. It’s small, but it is a fact about other people that RLS otherwise hides.
findings.repro: api-probes “the version counter is shared by everyone”
findings.evidence: A's version jumped from 0 to 43 for A's one change: B's 5 changes are visible as a gap of 42

findings.title: A notification whose text is over 8,000 characters (or expanded text over 16,000) is refused for ever
findings.detail: The server answers `malformed` and the shell marks it refused, so it never reaches `bank_events`. Raw text is meant to be stored first (§6.2). No bank sends that much today.
